newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Copper prices higher, agriculturals too.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Copper prices higher, agriculturals too.

text.p: LONDON, July 15 Reuter) - World copper prices surged higher on Monday on nearby supply concerns while hot weather sent Chicago grain markets spiralling higher.
Copper was the centre of attention on the London Metal Exchange (LME) with trade houses with commitments to the market through the middle of July finding supplies difficult to get hold of.
Those companies who held the metal were asking increasing premiums from those desparately seeking to cover their obligations.
This saw the price for prompt delivery copper soar to around $250 above the benchmark three months delivery position, which itself had risen over $30 from Friday's close.
LME chief-executive David King said that he continued to watch the copper market and noted that trading during the busy session was "totally orderly".
Another metal to attract buyers was zinc which moved above $1,500 a tonne for the first time for 6-3/4 years against a background of falling world stocks.
In Chicago the grain pits were hectic as concerns over reports of hot and dry weather in the U.S. Midwest over the week-end sent prices soaring.
"We are sharply higher because no rain means no grain," one Chicago floor trader said.
Extreme heat can hamper pollenation and most corn in the Midwest pollenates in July.
Corn was around nine cents a bushel up in early trade on Monday, wheat six cents and soyabeans streaked up the maximum permissible daily limit of 30 cents.
Warm weather in Brazil was having the opposite effect on coffee, down $40 a tonne in London, as it meant the likelihood of a winter frost was reducing daily, and the crop would be safe.
Also slower demand for coffee in Europe in the summer was forcing some large supermarket chains to destock which, in turn was slowing roaster demand for beans.
The gold market continued its stabilisation after the sell-off of the past two weeks.
Some physical demand lifted the price Monday morning but some producer sales appeared to put a lid on the market after it had risen around $2 an ounce.
